results.content:
A new Michigan State University survey shows Democrats leading in two of Michigan’s highest-profile 2026 races, adding to a series of recent polls that have shown similar advantages for the party’s nominees for governor and U.S. Senate.

According to results released Sept. 1 by MSU’s Institute for Public Policy and Social Research, Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson of Detroit leads U.S. Rep. John James of Shelby Township in the race for governor, 52% to 43% among likely voters.

results.content:
By the numbers: Since February, Republican consumer sentiment has plunged 15.1 index points, from 97.1 to 82, according to the latest University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers data. Democratic sentiment has fallen just 1.6 index points, from 41.8 to 40.2.

Republican consumer sentiment fell 15.1 points from February to August 2026, while Democratic sentiment fell 1.6 points over the same period.
